question: What kind of phyllotaxy was examined in the Guava plant?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Opposite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In an opposite phyllotaxy, two leaves arise at the same level from opposite sides of the stem.
 
• Each pair of leaves is typically perpendicular to the next pair above or below, providing a crisscross pattern.
 
• Opposite phyllotaxy ensures maximum light exposure for each leaf, which is beneficial for photosynthesis.
 
• This type of leaf arrangement is common in plants such as guava (Psidium guajava), calotropis, and jamun.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phyllotaxy**

 
 
• Phyllotaxy refers to the arrangement of leaves on a plant stem.
 
• The primary types of phyllotaxy are alternate, opposite, and whorled.
 
• This arrangement plays a significant role in maximizing light capture and minimizing shading of lower leaves.
 
 
 
• **Alternate Phyllotaxy**
 
 
• In alternate phyllotaxy, each leaf arises at a different level on the stem, and the leaves are not directly opposite each other.
 
• Examples include sunflower and mustard.
 
 
 
• **Whorled Phyllotaxy**
 
 
• In whorled phyllotaxy, three or more leaves grow at the same level around the stem.
 
• This arrangement is less common and can be seen in plants like Nerium (oleander).
